description.narrative:
The Project involves the construction of a new 75 kilometers (km) railway line between Hairatan at the border with Uzbekistan and Mazar-e-Sharif in Afghanistan. The Project represents a first phase of a larger rail network planned across the north and other parts of the country, including links to Herat, Tajikistan, and Pakistan. It will expand the existing transport network in Afghanistan and improve substantially internal and international connectivity. The Project is part of the Transport Strategy and Action Plan agreed under the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) Program. It will add capacity to two transport corridors under CAREC and open up alternative routes of supply for national and international trade, as well as for humanitarian relief to Afghanistan.
The Project has two components: (i) design and construction of 75 km single-line railway and associated infrastructure; and (ii) project management, independent supervision, and institutional support. The Project will be executed through a fixed price and fixed time delivery engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) turnkey contract. Once constructed, tested, and commissioned, the rail service will be managed by an operator under an operation and maintenance contract.

description.narrative: An efficient, safe, reliable railway transport network developed and operated in north Afghanistan.

By 2012: Reduced travel time for freight traffic between Hairatan and Mazar-e-Sharif to 1 hour from 2 hours in 2008 Progress/Status: The travel time for freight transportation by rail between Hairatan and Mazar-e-Sharif has been reduced to about 1 hour. Data Source: Statistics from Ministry of Commerce, Traffic surveys by railway department, MPW (upon Project completion) Actual value:

By 2012: CO2 emission reduction from 2.3 million ton (2008) to 1.7 million ton Progress/Status: CO2 emissions are about 1.9 million tons per year at current volumes of freight traffic. At 2008 volumes of traffic, emissions have been reduced to less than 1.7 million tons. Data Source: Traffic surveys by railway department, MPW (upon Project completion) Actual value:

By 2012: Freight transported by trains reached 6,000 ton per day from 4,500 ton per day in 2008 Progress/Status: Freight transported by trains reached about 6,500 tons per day in 2012. Data Source: Statistics from Ministry of Commerce Actual value:

By 2012: Composition of heavy vehicle traffic on Hairatan-Mazar-e-Sharif road reduced to 35% from 50% in 2008 Progress/Status: The composition of heavy vehicle traffic is about 40%, at current volumes of freight traffic. At 2008 volumes of traffic, the composition is less than 35%. Data Source: Statistics from Ministry of Commerce, Traffic surveys by railway department, MPW (upon Project completion) Actual value:

By 2012: Increased job opportunities for women in the rail service and local businesses, including logistics services at all stations and airport at Mazar-e-Sharif Progress/Status: Employment in the project area has shown an overall growth of 10-11% per year. About 1,200 local people have been employed in logistics and unloading operations in Hairatan and Naibabad. However, due to cultural restrictions, the number of women employed is insignificant. More employment opportunities will arise, including for women, with the expansion of facilities and businesses at Naibabad. Data Source: Statistics from Ministry of Commerce, Employment statistics in Balkh Province Base year: 2008

By 2012: Reduced incidence of HIV/AIDS and sexually transmitted diseases in the Project area Progress/Status: About 29 suspected cases of HIV and other sexually transmitted infections have been reported in Balkh Province, of which none relate to the Hairatan-Mazar-e-Sharif project area. Data Source: Statistics from health agency in Balkh Province Base year: 2008
